description: Width tiers for Health and Physical Education, Years 9-10. Covers all 19 descriptors across the Movement and Physical Activity strand and the Personal, Social and Community Health strand.
subject: Health and Physical Education

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term in a single context. For health standards: engaging with one scenario, one strategy, or one form of bias/media message. For movement standards: performing or analysing in one familiar or semi-familiar activity type. Minimum must genuinely satisfy the descriptor's command term — 'evaluate' requires evaluation, 'critique' requires critique, not just description.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope across the range of contexts ACARA's elaborations indicate. For health standards: engaging with multiple scenario types, relationship contexts, or community situations. For movement standards: applying skills or strategies across several activity types or conditions. What a well-taught class engaging the full elaboration set would reach.
width_notes.wider: Additional task contexts, community settings, cultural frameworks, or challenge types beyond the typical elaboration set. Must add a genuinely different context — not a harder version of the same context. First Nations Australian contexts appear in wider wherever elaborations include them — these are substantive enrichment directions, not optional extras.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as primary source data for scoping typical_width and generating wider directions.

AC9HP10P01.minimum_width: Identify at least two societal or cultural factors that influence identity; analyse their influence in one specific context; describe one way an individual (family, friend, community) influences another's identity.
AC9HP10P01.typical_width: Analyse how societal norms, stereotypes and cultural expectations shape how young people view themselves across multiple contexts; analyse the role of family, friends and community in supporting individual identities; propose strategies to enhance their own and others' wellbeing; examine how societal expectations influence perceptions of movement competence.
wider: Analyse how personal totems in First Nations Australian cultures contribute to identity, comparing this with identity markers in other cultural traditions
Investigate how cultural beliefs and practices surrounding transitions to adulthood differ across cultures including cultures of Asia, and what this reveals about identity construction
Examine how changing social standing within First Nations Australian communities alters identity and evaluate culturally appropriate support strategies
elaborations: evaluating how societal norms, stereotypes and expectations influence how young people view themselves and how they deal with these influences
analysing how the use of personal totems in First Nations Australian cultures can be based on personal qualities and contribute to identities
investigating how cultural beliefs and practices surrounding transitions to adulthood may differ between cultures, including the cultures of Asia
analysing the role of family, friends and community in supporting an individual's identities, and proposing strategies to enhance their own and others' wellbeing
examining how societal norms, stereotypes and expectations influence perceptions of movement competence

AC9HP10P02.minimum_width: Evaluate the effectiveness of one strategy for managing a change or transition in a specific situation; identify what worked and what did not.
AC9HP10P02.typical_width: Assess behavioural expectations across different relationships and social situations; evaluate how these influence decisions during transitions; practise refusal skills, communicating choices, expressing opinions and contingency planning; rehearse asserting a stance while acknowledging others' feelings.
wider: Analyse changing roles and responsibilities for First Nations Australians as social standing changes within communities — evaluate culturally appropriate versus externally imposed strategies
Investigate the impact of border crossing on identity for First Nations Australians and evaluate specific strategies for navigating between cultural contexts
Evaluate strategies for managing digital transitions and contemporary online identity shifts as a distinct transition category
elaborations: practising skills to deal with challenging or unsafe situations, such as refusal skills, communicating choices, expressing opinions and initiating contingency plans
assessing behavioural expectations in different relationships and social situations, and examining how these expectations can influence decisions and actions
analysing the changing roles and responsibilities for First Nations Australians as their social standing changes within their communities
discussing the impact of border crossing on the development of identities for First Nations Australians
rehearsing strategies to respectfully assert their stance on a situation, dilemma or decision by expressing thoughts, opinions and beliefs that acknowledge the feelings of others

AC9HP10P03.minimum_width: Identify at least two attitudes that enable gender-based violence and explain the mechanism; explain one way gender equality reduces conditions for violence or coercion.
AC9HP10P03.typical_width: Analyse attitudes that lead to enacting, excusing or condoning gender-based violence; evaluate how gender equality empowers equal and respectful relationships; examine intergenerational patterns of gender inequality and propose community-level prevention strategies.
wider: Explore how gender inequality arises from intergenerational patterns of inequity in specific scenarios and propose strategies for challenging inequality in communities
Investigate how media representations normalise attitudes that condone gender-based violence — evaluate using evidence
Investigate how First Nations communities have developed gender equity approaches that reflect cultural sovereignty — evaluate how these complement mainstream prevention frameworks
elaborations: investigate and challenge attitudes that lead to people enacting, excusing or condoning gender-based violence
analysing ways that attitudes towards gender equality and power can affect expectations and behaviour, and lead to practices of sexual coercion, harassment, violence and submission
evaluating how gender equality can empower people to develop equal and respectful relationships

exploring scenarios in texts that demonstrate how gender inequality can arise from intergenerational patterns of inequity and unequal power in relationships, and proposing strategies for challenging inequality in their communities

AC9HP10P04.minimum_width: Identify a power imbalance in a relationship and evaluate its effect on one party's autonomy; explain one way respect or empathy strengthens a relationship.
AC9HP10P04.typical_width: Investigate how power balance influences relationships; evaluate rights and ethical responsibilities in relationships; investigate characteristics of positive respectful relationships; examine bullying, racism and gender-based violence in face-to-face and online environments; propose actions when relationships become coercive.
wider: Investigate how historical patterns of inequity have lasting intergenerational effects on wellbeing — evaluate strategies for building cultural awareness contributing to reconciliation
Investigate how demonstrating support for truth-telling causes builds cultural awareness and empathy at community level
Evaluate how cultural practices of respect and empathy differ across communities and what this means for cross-cultural relationships
elaborations: investigating the characteristics of positive, respectful relationships and the rights and ethical responsibilities of individuals in relationships
investigating how the balance of power influences the nature of relationships and proposing actions that can be taken when a relationship is not respectful
investigating how demonstrating support for causes that promote truth-telling can build cultural awareness, empathy and respectful relationships
identifying the ways in which historical patterns of inequity, violence and discrimination can have lasting intergenerational effects on wellbeing
investigating how bullying, racism and gender-based violence can take different forms, including verbal, physical, emotional, sexual and economic forms, in both face-to-face and online environments

AC9HP10P05.minimum_width: Identify one form of bias or discrimination and analyse how it operates; propose one strategy that addresses its mechanism.
AC9HP10P05.typical_width: Analyse implications of prejudice, marginalisation, homophobia, racism, discrimination on individuals and communities; critique media representations of cultural groups; analyse gender norm messaging in popular culture; design strategies to challenge stereotypes and acknowledge First Nations Australians' contributions; propose strategies against biases targeting Australians of Asian heritage.
wider: Investigate community health resources for marginalised groups — evaluate accessibility and propose improvements
Critique a specific media representation of a First Nations Australian community for respect, realism and inclusiveness
Investigate bystander intervention programs as an inclusion strategy — evaluate conditions for effectiveness and barriers
elaborations: analysing the implications of attitudes and behaviours such as prejudice, marginalisation, homophobia, racism, discrimination, violence and harassment on individuals and communities
investigating community health resources to evaluate how accessible they are for marginalised individuals and groups
critiquing media representations of different cultural and racial groups
analysing messages about gender norms and stereotypes in popular culture
designing strategies to challenge stereotypes, prejudices and discrimination, and publicly acknowledge the contributions First Nations Australians make to Australia's sporting and health fields
proposing strategies to challenge prejudices, biases and discrimination that target specific cultural groups, including Australians of Asian heritage

AC9HP10P06.minimum_width: Identify one emotional response in a specific situation and evaluate its consequences; identify one refinement to a prior emotion management strategy.
AC9HP10P06.typical_width: Reflect on consequences of unrecognised emotions in challenging situations including rejection, failure, harassment and violence; evaluate situations with extreme or uncontrolled emotional responses and their relational impact; propose refined strategies across family, school, social and online environments.
wider: Evaluate conflict escalation case studies — trace emotional responses and identify where different responses could have changed outcomes
Analyse emotional responses in online environments and evaluate whether face-to-face strategies transfer
Evaluate consequences of emotional responses in physical activity contexts — frustration, aggression, and team dynamics
elaborations: proposing strategies for managing emotional responses and resolving conflict in a family, school or social situation, or online environment
reflecting on the possible consequences of not recognising their own or others' emotions in challenging situations, including responses to rejection, failure, harassment and violence
evaluating situations where an individual may react with extreme or uncontrolled emotion and reflecting on the impact on the situation and relationships

AC9HP10P07.minimum_width: Describe one consent communication strategy in a specific scenario; explain one way consent communication supports a more respectful relationship.
AC9HP10P07.typical_width: Refine strategies for communicating choices, needs and opinions across peer, family and work situations; describe strategies for sexual partner safety including affirmative consent and assertive communication; reflect on responsibility for own behaviour; examine how consent communication connects to respectful relationships broadly and sexual relationships specifically.
wider: Investigate legal requirements for consent (state/territory) across relationship types and contexts including online — evaluate how these laws connect to respectful relationship principles
Rehearse consent communication under social pressure or power imbalance conditions
Examine how consent portrayal in TV, movies, popular music and online content influences beliefs about respectful consensual relationships
elaborations: describing strategies that enhance the safety and wellbeing of sexual partners, including affirmative consent, assertive communication and respecting rights
investigating the legal requirements for consent in relation to seeking, giving, refusing and accepting refusal of consent in online and offline interactions
reflecting on the potential impact of own behaviour on others and taking responsibility for own actions
refining strategies to communicate clearly and respectfully choices, needs and opinions in peer group, family or work situations

AC9HP10P08.minimum_width: Identify one health risk situation and plan a realistic response; rehearse the response and evaluate its effectiveness.
AC9HP10P08.typical_width: Plan and rehearse responses across multiple risk situations including peer pressure (substance use), first aid emergencies (CPR), and digital safety; critique appropriateness of community support services; evaluate realistic refusal skills; investigate safe blood practices and consent under impairment.
wider: Plan and practise refusal skill scenarios across e-cigarettes, cannabis, psychostimulants, opiates and hallucinogens — evaluate which approaches are most realistic in peer contexts
Practise and evaluate CPR and basic first aid against criteria — identify what further practice is needed
Evaluate digital safety resources and support services for young people in your community
elaborations: critiquing the appropriateness and effectiveness of help and support services for young people
proposing and practising realistic responses to scenarios involving peer pressure around substance use
investigating safe, legal and ethical behaviour in digital environments
planning and practising responses to emergencies including CPR
understanding factors impacting ability to consent when affected by alcohol or other drugs
examining safe blood practices across multiple situations

AC9HP10P09.minimum_width: Apply at least two criteria to critique one piece of health information or media messaging; identify its likely influence on attitudes.
AC9HP10P09.typical_width: Critique health information and services across multiple domains (substance use, food, fitness, mental health, sexual health, personal safety); critique sexual relationship portrayals in TV, advertising, movies, music and online content for influence on consent beliefs; evaluate strategies for personal safety.
wider: Analyse nutritional composition of foods eaten by First Peoples of Australia and evaluate how this could increase health benefits — assess how this knowledge has been presented in mainstream health media
Investigate health issues specific to First Nations Australian communities and critique mainstream messaging for relevance and accessibility
Design a counter-messaging strategy for misleading health information targeting a specific audience
elaborations: critiquing health information and services for young people across substance use, food choices, fitness, mental health, sexual health and personal safety
analysing nutritional composition of foods eaten by First Peoples of Australia
evaluating strategies to increase personal safety
investigating health issues specific to First Nations Australian communities and proposing proactive community strategies
discussing how portrayals of sexual relationships in media may influence beliefs about respectful, safe and consensual relationships

AC9HP10P10.minimum_width: Plan one strategy for a specific health or wellbeing outcome with at least one justified reason; apply two criteria to critique it.
AC9HP10P10.typical_width: Plan and justify strategies across individual and community levels; consider social, cultural and economic factors affecting health behaviours and help-seeking; design mental health and wellbeing strategies; evaluate stigma's effect on help-seeking for mental health, sexual health and other sensitive areas; propose constructive digital health promotion actions.
wider: Investigate cultural rights of First Nations Australians to maintain traditional diets — critique mainstream health strategies for whether they address this right
Investigate the pharmacopeia and health practices of First Nations Australian communities (respecting ICIP protocols) and evaluate how these could inform broader community health strategies
Evaluate how stigma associated with specific health issues affects help-seeking — critique current stigma-reduction strategies and propose targeted improvements
elaborations: investigating community-action initiatives young people have started with positive health and wellbeing influence
proposing, sharing and evaluating sustainable food preparation presentations
exploring how connection to Country/Place enhances health and wellbeing for First Nations Australians
investigating cultural rights of First Nations Australians to maintain traditional diets
analysing social, cultural and economic factors influencing health behaviours and help-seeking
investigating First Nations Australian community pharmacopeia and health practices with respect for ICIP protocols
proposing constructive digital health promotion actions
designing and evaluating mental health and wellbeing strategies

AC9HP10M01.minimum_width: Identify at least two specific aspects of a movement performance that affect the outcome; make one adaptation based on analysis and evaluate whether it improved the outcome.
AC9HP10M01.typical_width: Use knowledge of results and digital tools to analyse and refine performance across multiple activity types; provide and act on constructive peer feedback; analyse performances at swimming, cross-country or athletics contexts and propose refinement strategies; adapt in response to equipment changes.
wider: Use video analysis to compare own performance against a reference model — identify timing or technique differences and explain their effect
Analyse performance changes with different equipment types — evaluate which adaptations improve performance and why
Lead a peer refinement session with structured feedback — evaluate whether feedback produced measurable change
elaborations: using knowledge of results feedback to support skill refinement for greater accuracy and control
using digital tools to record performance and provide feedback on timing relative to teammates and external stimuli
adapting and responding to equipment changes that increase movement complexity
analysing performances at swimming, cross-country or athletics and proposing refinement strategies
providing constructive feedback on group performance of movement sequences

AC9HP10M02.minimum_width: Create one movement strategy with a stated intended outcome and explicit reasoning; evaluate it against at least one self-developed criterion.
AC9HP10M02.typical_width: Create movement strategies responding to specific situational demands; implement alternative responses based on previous performance outcomes; perform specialised skills in modified-rule situations; evaluate effectiveness using personally developed criteria; adapt strategies using different equipment types.
wider: Develop a multi-criteria evaluation framework and apply across two or more different game situations
Use digital performance data to evaluate strategy effectiveness — refine based on data rather than subjective impression
Evaluate a peer's strategy using their own criteria — provide feedback on the gap between intended and actual outcomes
elaborations: reviewing, proposing and implementing alternative responses based on previous performance outcomes
performing specialised movement skills in modified-rule situations
adapting and refining strategies with different equipment types
evaluating effectiveness of strategies using personally developed criteria and suggesting adaptations

AC9HP10M03.minimum_width: Apply one movement concept deliberately in a new or challenging situation; analyse its impact on the movement outcome.
AC9HP10M03.typical_width: Apply movement concepts in new or challenging situations; experiment with force and speed manipulation for different movement paths; analyse force absorption techniques for injury prevention; create and evaluate group performances with synchronous and individual movements; analyse space and time modifications and their performance impact.
wider: Apply force manipulation concepts across two or more sport types — compare how the same concept operates differently with different equipment
Analyse force absorption across multiple game situations — evaluate which techniques are most effective and connect to injury prevention
Conduct systematic personal performance analysis — trace concept impact at each phase and propose refinements
elaborations: experimenting with force and speed manipulation to examine differences in movement paths
analysing body force absorption techniques and evaluating effectiveness for injury prevention across game situations
creating and evaluating group performances with synchronous and individual movements
analysing how space and time modifications improve individual or team performance

AC9HP10M04.minimum_width: Participate in a physical activity and identify at least two physiological responses; design a personalised plan with one justified goal and evaluate it after implementation.
AC9HP10M04.typical_width: Evaluate individual physiological responses across multiple activity types; analyse how activities improve specific fitness components; set realistic goals; design, implement and evaluate a personalised program using digital tools; justify activity selections against goals.
wider: Incorporate target heart-rate zones into a multi-week plan — justify intensity choices against specific fitness component goals
Evaluate a multi-week plan with documented adjustments — track what factors supported or hindered adherence
Design a personalised plan for a different person — justify adaptations and evaluate what personalisation required
elaborations: participating in physical activities and evaluating individual responses including heart rate, breathing rate and recovery rate
performing fitness activities and analysing how they improve fitness components
setting realistic physical activity goals and designing, implementing and evaluating a personalised program

AC9HP10M05.minimum_width: Participate in one physical activity with a social dimension; identify one health and one social outcome; design one participation strategy for a named target group.
AC9HP10M05.typical_width: Participate in activities promoting health and social outcomes; identify community spaces for physical and social connection; investigate community campaigns; create proposals for natural setting use; design strategies involving family, friends and community in culturally significant activities.
wider: Investigate how culturally significant physical activities create community connection — evaluate social outcomes beyond physical health
Design a participation strategy for a specific community group (elderly, CALD) — justify design choices for that group
Create a community celebration proposal based around culturally significant physical activities — evaluate how it promotes belonging for diverse community members
elaborations: creating and evaluating proposals to promote use of natural settings for physical activity
designing strategies involving family, friends and community in culturally significant physical activity celebrations
investigating community-based campaigns and determining key success elements
identifying local natural resources and community spaces for physical and social activity

AC9HP10M06.minimum_width: Design a personalised plan with at least two justified activity selections; implement for a defined period and evaluate against the goal.
AC9HP10M06.typical_width: Design using digital tools with timeframe, goals and variety of activities; justify selections linked to goals and wellbeing outcomes; investigate target heart-rate zones; implement, monitor and evaluate; make documented adjustments.
wider: Track multi-week implementation with digital tools — evaluate adherence patterns and make justified adjustments based on data
Evaluate a plan designed for another person — assess whether it met their needs and what the evaluation reveals about designing effective plans for others
Compare outcomes from two different plan designs (high frequency/low intensity vs low frequency/high intensity) for the same individual
elaborations: using digital tools to design, implement and monitor a personal fitness plan with timeframe, goals and varied activities
justifying activity selections linked to physical activity goals and wellbeing outcomes
investigating target training heart-rate zones for different people and how they relate to health and fitness

AC9HP10M07.minimum_width: Identify one skill or strategy from a familiar context and explain which elements transfer to a named unfamiliar situation; apply the transfer and evaluate whether it was successful.
AC9HP10M07.typical_width: Draw parallels between strategies across different sports; apply transfer thinking to outdoor or nature-based activities; reflect on effectiveness of transfer solutions and propose how they can be applied to further situations.
wider: Systematically map transferable skills across two or more sport or movement contexts — identify what transfers directly, what needs adaptation, and what is genuinely new
Evaluate a failed transfer attempt — identify what was wrongly assumed to transfer and propose what would need to be different
Lead a group through an unfamiliar movement challenge using deliberate transfer thinking — evaluate the group's success
elaborations: drawing parallels between successful movement strategies across different sports
speculating on outcomes of innovative solutions based on past experience in outdoor or nature-based activities
reflecting on effectiveness of movement solutions and proposing how they can be transferred to other situations

AC9HP10M08.minimum_width: Demonstrate fair play in one physical activity context; identify one contested ethical issue in sport and reflect on how competing positions influence outcomes.
AC9HP10M08.typical_width: Demonstrate fair play across contexts; analyse equitable participation and its influence on outcomes; analyse First Nations Australian athletes' treatment and its impact on young people's participation; investigate PED debates and competing positions; discuss role of sport integrity organisations.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian athletes have navigated inequitable treatment — evaluate how their responses modelled ethical behaviour and influenced cultural change
Construct an evidence-based argument for one position on PEDs and evaluate the strongest counterargument
Investigate a specific case resolved by a sporting tribunal — evaluate how the resolution influenced ethical standards in that sport
elaborations: analysing how equitable participation in group activities influences outcomes
investigating performance-enhancing drugs and tensions between competing positions
discussing the role of Sports Integrity Australia, sporting tribunals, the Australian Human Rights Commission and the Court of Arbitration for Sport
analysing how First Nations Australian athletes have been treated and evaluating impacts on young First Nations Australians' participation

AC9HP10M09.minimum_width: Devise one decision-making strategy for a group context; implement it and evaluate one specific aspect of how it performed.
AC9HP10M09.typical_width: Devise and implement decision-making strategies across group and team contexts; use self-assessment and peer-assessment tools to evaluate performance in multiple roles; apply self-talk and encouragement; evaluate own contribution to teamwork quality and enjoyment.
wider: Implement the same decision-making strategy across two different group contexts and evaluate how it needed to be adapted for each
Create a peer-assessment tool for leadership and collaboration — use peer feedback to refine own leadership approach
Document the decision-making process in real time during a group initiative — evaluate the gap between devised strategy and actual practice
elaborations: evaluating own contribution to teamwork, leadership and enjoyable participation
analysing self-talk and encouragement to motivate team members and improve performance
creating and implementing self-assessment and peer-assessment tools to evaluate performance in multiple roles
identifying and critiquing leadership styles and group dynamics through initiative games
